title: Task Envelope v1
description: The unit of work handed to an agentic implementation run. One envelope produces at most one pull request. The envelope is authored by a human, validated deterministically, and reproduced verbatim into the PR body so downstream metrics can be extracted without re-reading the source issue.

envelope_version.description: Schema major version. Bumped only on a breaking field change; metrics.sh keys off this.

task_id.description: Stable identifier for this task, unique per repository. GitHub spine: gh-<issue number>. Linear spine: the Linear issue identifier (e.g. ENG-482). Used as the dedup key so a re-run cannot open a second PR for the same task.

title.description: One-line imperative summary. Becomes the PR title after the title-prefix.

risk_tier.description: Review tier. T1: mechanical, reversible, single-file-shaped. T2: ordinary feature or fix inside one service. T3: touches a contract, a privilege boundary, data, or money. See README section 6.

engine.description: Which coding engine executes the implement node. Selected per task from day one; the two engines are compared on identical metrics.

blueprint.description: The node sequence that will run. Only implement-v1 exists in W1-2.

profile.description: Repository sub-target this task belongs to. Monorepo: the service or package name. Single-service repo: omit, or use the repo's own short name. Drives which test target the affected-tests node resolves.

goal.description: What must become true, and why. Prose, not a task list. The agent is expected to reason from this rather than from the title.

non_goals.description: Explicitly out of scope. The single highest-value field for keeping an agent inside the intended blast radius.

acceptance_criteria.description: Observable conditions a reviewer can check without reading the diff. Each item must be falsifiable.

allowed_paths.description: Glob patterns the patch may touch. Empty means the repository default allowlist applies. Enforced by the envelope-guard required check against the PR's changed-file list, NOT by the agent's own restraint. Required (>= 1 entry) when risk_tier is T3.

test_command.description: The command the affected-tests node runs. Repo-relative, no sudo, must exit non-zero on failure. Use the repo's affected-test target when it has one (e.g. make test-affected).

source_url.description: URL of the human-authored design note, ADR, or RFC that justifies the change. Required when risk_tier is T3: a T3 task without a written design note is a design task, not an implementation task.

context_refs.description: Paths or URLs the agent should read before writing code. Keep to files that actually constrain the change; AGENTS.md is already loaded as the index.

rollback.description: How to undo this change in production if it misbehaves. Free text; 'revert the PR' is an acceptable answer when it is actually true.

max_ci_fix_rounds.description: Hard cap on agentic CI-fix attempts. The blueprint constant is 2; a task may lower it, never raise it.

import_from.description: Makes this an L4 import task: no agent runs. A trusted job copies the named files of another repository at one commit, by (mode, OID), and opens the PR itself (scripts/import_verify.py). The path grammar beyond these patterns (no `.`, `..` or `.git` component, a directory only maps to a directory, unique case-folded destinations, no protected destination) is checked by import_verify.grammar_errors, which the validator also runs.

repo.description: OWNER/NAME of the source. Must also be a line of vars.IMPORT_ALLOWED_REPOS.

ref.description: The full commit SHA. No tag, no branch: the pair repo@ref must be a line of vars.IMPORT_PINS.

map.description: `from -> to` pairs. A trailing slash marks a directory, which maps every file under it.

max_ai_credits.description: Optional per-run AI Credit budget override passed to the runner. Omit to inherit the workflow default.

allOf.description: T3 conditional rules: a T3 task must name its design note and must bound its blast radius explicitly.
